title: Bahia Advance to Women's Brasileirão Semifinals After Penalty Shootout Victory
subtitle: Goalkeeper Yanne Lopes and tailored preparation were decisive in qualification
excerpt: Bahia beat Palmeiras on penalties to reach the club's first Women's Brasileirão semifinal, highlighting Yanne Lopes' performance and intense training.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Bahia overcame Palmeiras on penalties to secure the first semifinal spot for a northeastern club in the Campeonato Brasileiro Feminino. The clash, decided 5-4 following a 1-1 draw in regulation time, put goalkeeper Yanne Lopes in the spotlight.

How the match against Palmeiras unfolded

The matchup ended in a 1-1 draw in both the first leg at Arena Fonte Nova and the return leg at Arena Barueri. Raíssa opened the scoring for Palmeiras, but Dan Nunes equalized for Bahia shortly after. In the second half, Dan scored again following an assist from Roqueline, sealing the draw.

Yanne Lopes' decisive role in the shootout

During the penalty shootout, head coach Felipe Freitas put his trust in the goalkeeper, stating that she "is the face" of saves. Yanne stopped the spot-kick from Tainá Maranhão, while her teammates converted all of their attempts. The save was crucial to the 5-4 final score.

Intensive penalty training at Bahia

Felipe Freitas revealed that the squad practiced 2,632 penalties throughout the season, averaging roughly 15.2 per training session. Goalkeeping coach André Cainã highlighted that the work includes chaotic scenarios and opposition analysis using tools like Wyscout and Sports Coder.

The impact of goalkeeper preparation

Beyond Yanne's save, the goalkeepers' preparation includes strength, power, and decision-making drills amidst multiple balls. Cainã emphasized that technical development and footwork are becoming increasingly vital in women's football.

Bahia's next challenges

With the qualification, Bahia will await the winner of the tie between Cruzeiro and Corinthians to determine their next opponent. The Bahia side shows confidence in continuing their penalty routines and in the structure provided by the club, which shares resources with the men's team.

With reporting from ge, UOL, VEJA.
